rgb: This indoor living space is seen from the downward-looking perspective of a seated camera wearer. No one else is present; only the wearer’s lap, hands, and bare feet appear along the bottom. Immediately beneath the viewpoint, about 0.4 to 0.6 metres away and comfortably within arm’s reach, a rectangular metal tray filled with shelled green peas sits on the wearer’s red-and-white patterned lap between the chair’s wooden armrests. Roughly 1.0 to 1.5 metres ahead, just beyond ordinary seated reach, a small dark wooden side table stands to the front-left with two remote controls and an orange pen on top. It is approximately 0.3 to 0.5 metres left of a cushioned sofa at the front-right, which carries a green patterned bag, a white plastic bag, and several small dark objects. Over the five frames, the wearer’s viewpoint pivots slightly to the right, so a plaid-covered item of furniture at the far-left edge, around 0.5 metres away, disappears entirely after frame 2 while a larger portion of the right-side sofa enters view. At the same time, the wearer lifts a blue plastic bag containing pea pods from the left side of the lap in frames 1 and 2, raises and shifts it across the lap’s centre in frame 3, temporarily blocking the metal tray below, and sets it down to the right of the wooden armrest in frames 4 and 5, about 0.5 metres from the viewpoint and 0.2 metres right of the tray. The wearer’s lower legs, the chair back, and the outer edges of both the sofa and side table stay partly hidden or cut off by the image boundaries throughout.
depth: The depth view depicts the seated camera wearer looking downward at their lap and hands, which are the brightest regions at approximately 0.2–0.6 m away. A rectangular metal tray holding shelled peas lies on the thighs at about 0.5 m between the chair armrests. Farther away, a small wooden side table occupies the upper left and a cushioned sofa the upper right, both around 1.0–1.8 m distant, with roughly 0.5 m of floor between them at a depth of about 1.5–2.0 m. There are no other people. The wearer’s hands, the lap tray, and a blue plastic bag containing pea pods are all directly reachable, whereas the nearby furniture is just outside normal reach and partly cut off at the frame borders. Through frames 1–2, the blue bag begins on the left thigh at roughly 0.5 m; in frame 3 it is raised close to the camera at about 0.2–0.3 m and blocks the tray and lap; and in frames 4–5 it moves across to the right side at approximately 0.5–0.7 m while the camera turns slightly rightward. Compared with the flat overhead RGB view, the depth rendering distinguishes the vertical spacing among the elevated hands and bag, the tray surface, and the lower floor more clearly. Its output becomes unreliable during the rapid movement in frame 3, however, when the motion-blurred hands and bag combine into an unclear white mass, and it loses subtle 3D features such as separate peas and the small items on the more distant table and sofa.
segmentation: The instance-segmentation output misses nearly all of the room’s arrangement: in frames 1–3 and 5 it omits the furniture, floor, blue plastic bag, and camera wearer’s body, identifying only separate foreground areas on the wearer’s lap approximately 0.4–0.6 m away. More precisely, it marks the mound of green peas on the tray in frames 1, 2, and 4, directly in front of the wearer and within reach; creates two overlapping masks over the metal tray around the peas in frame 4; and shows one mask on the wearer’s left forearm at the bottom-centre of frame 5, about 0.4 m away. No other people appear or face the camera. Every detection disappears in frame 3 as the moving blue bag covers the tray. Once the bag shifts right, detections return over the tray and peas in the lower left of frame 4, then decline to only the left forearm in frame 5. The crisp mask outlines in frames 1, 2, and 4 do help separate the boundary of the pea pile from the reflective tray, but the map remains highly unreliable. It incorrectly labels the shelled peas as “broccoli,” treats the flat rectangular tray as two overlapping “bowl” instances, entirely misses the peas in frame 5, and does not segment the wearer’s hands or legs or any furniture in the background.
pose: The pose output contains only magenta 2D hand skeletons on an entirely black background, so it conveys nothing about the spatial arrangement of the room, its furniture or objects, or any additional people. Only the camera wearer is present, facing downward toward their lap. Frame 1 detects just the wearer’s right hand, around 0.4–0.5 m from the camera in the lower-left of the strip’s first frame. Frame 2 instead detects only the left hand gripping the bag on the left at about 0.4–0.5 m. Both hands are working immediately above the lap within easy arm’s reach, while the remainder of the wearer’s body is either unseen or not detected. During the quick lift and rightward movement of the blue bag, the skeletons vanish entirely in frames 3 and 4. In frame 5, one skeleton returns for the left hand resting by the tray’s edge at roughly 0.4 m in the centre-left, while the right hand holding the bag at the far right is not detected. In frames 1, 2, and 5, the articulated finger landmarks reveal the precise bend and direction of the curled fingers more clearly than the motion-blurred RGB imagery. Overall, though, the pose map is very unreliable: it omits every yellow body keypoint, including the wrists, forearms, and thighs, in all frames; loses one hand in frames 1, 2, and 5; and detects neither hand in frames 3 or 4 because of motion blur and self-occlusion involving the plastic bag.
